editorial:
You follow Abel Morales, an immigrant businessman in New York City during the brutal winter of 1981. He runs a heating oil company and wants to grow it by buying a new storage facility. But his trucks keep getting hijacked, his drivers are scared, and a district attorney is investigating his business. His wife Anna, who comes from a mob-connected family, pushes him to fight back harder. The movie feels tense and grounded, more like a slow-burn drama than a shoot-em-up.

Oscar Isaac gives a strong, quiet performance as a man trying to stay honest in a dirty world. Jessica Chastain is fierce as his wife. The pacing is slow but deliberate, building pressure scene by scene. The downside is it can feel too slow if you want action. If you like character-driven crime stories like The Godfather or Michael Clayton, you'll enjoy this. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Abel finally closes the deal on the storage facility after a tense negotiation. He discovers Anna has been cooking the books and hiding money, but he accepts it to protect the business. The DA's case weakens. Abel gets what he wanted, but at a moral cost, showing how the city's corruption slowly pulls even a principled man into compromise.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven crime dramas and slow-burn thrillers.
